Online Assessment


4th August,2023

20,50 & 50  respectively. 
Power Limit  - 20 points
Given 2 resources with powers A and B respectively. At each second, you have to select one resource
out of 2 to run the software. The power of the resource at the time of selection should be greater than 1.
Every second, the power of the selected resource gets reduced by 2 and the power of unselected
resource gets charged by 1. The software stops when at least one resource has 0 power.
You are given integers A and B.
Print the maximum number of seconds your software can run if you select the resources optimally.
Complete the function PowerLimit(). 
This function takes the following 2 parameters and returns the required answer:
• A: Représents the power of the first resource
• B: Represents the power of the second resource
Auto Suggest - 50 points
N: Represents the number of words in the dictionary
words: Represents the dictionary
S: Represents the query word
Given a dictionary consisting of N words and a query word S. You need to auto-suggest the best word
from the dictionary that is closest to S.Two words are first compared by their Levenshtein distance to the
word S. If two words have the same Levenshtein distance, then the lexicographically smaller word is
given priority.
• Levenshtein distance between two strings is defined as the minimum number of edits required to
obtain one string from the other. An "edit" is defined by either an insertion of a character, a deletion of a
character, or a replacement of a character.
All the words and the query word S consist of lowercase alphabets only.

Backlink Sorting - 50 points
WebPage: Represents an array of strings that contains the webpage titles
Backlinks: Represents an array of integers that contains the backlink count

web page. The objective is to rank the web pages in descending order based on the number of
backlinks they have.
Note: If two or more web pages have the same number of backlinks, maintain their original order.

Tips
Related to DSA
Data Structures & Algorithms : 450dsa (recommended) or striver’s list
1. Keep some hard copies of your resume handy. Since some companies take offline
interviews, they do ask for hard copies.
2. Be very thorough with your CS fundamentals. Don’t neglect it and leave it for the end.
3. When you don’t understand a particular problem statement, do ask for clarifications on it.
4. Think out loud. This way the interviewer gets an idea about which direction you are
headed and may help you start thinking in the right direction. This also keeps the interview
interactive.
5. Make sure to go through all projects on your resume and be prepared for questions that
can be asked about them like why did you use this technology/framework instead of that
technology/framework, difference between two frameworks, etc.
6. It is alright to tell them that you don’t know a particular thing instead of bluffing about it
and getting caught. They don’t expect you to know everything. They are more interested in
seeing how you use the knowledge you have and apply your logic to tackle an unseen
problem statement.
Lastly, keep calm during your interviews and have confidence in yourself.
                                                     All the best !!👍

OneNote/Notion/Docs (not traditional notes but screenshots would do - screenshots helped
me a lot during revision). For OOPS, use any resource available online in your language of
choice (prefer C++, Java or Python) and cover the major concepts in it.
